pills.pop_html: What kids do: Roll pre-prepared dough into strips, wrap it around a wooden spindle, brush it with sugar and watch it caramelise in a rotating oven. The dough needs about 75 minutes to rise, so it is ready when you arrive.

pills.summary_html: 👨‍👧 1 adult per 4 kids▾
pills.pop_html: Age rule: For every 4 children one adult has to join the activity. No minimum age is stated, and the listing pitches it at families, couples and small groups.
Timing: About 45 minutes of hands-on baking, then 20 minutes to eat your chimney cake with coffee or tea. Everyone gets a certificate of completion at the end.
Allergies: The small shared space uses wheat (gluten), orange, milk, nuts and coconut, and these cannot be removed. Children with any of these allergies should not attend.

best_for.pick_html: for families with kids of mixed ages because everyone bakes, eats and takes home a certificate in 65 minutes for about €20 a head.
best_for.skip_html: if anyone in the family is allergic to gluten, milk, nuts, orange or coconut: the shared kitchen cannot rule them out.

items.a: All ingredients and tools, hands-on workshop, apron, one freshly baked chimney cake, toppings, certificate of completion, coffee or tea.
One adult required for every 4 children.
15 minutes from the centre by public transport. Not safe for several common allergies. Instruction in English.
Hands-on from start to finish, dough already risen. Toppings, apron, coffee or tea and a certificate included. Short enough for younger attention spans.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

pills.pop_html: What you play: Machines from the 1800s through to modern tables, including the first flipper machine from the 1940s. You can play everything except Hercules, the world's biggest pinball machine, which is there for selfies.
How the ticket works: A bracelet lets you leave and come back as often as you like on the same night, so you can go out for dinner and return.
Hours: You can play right up to midnight, which makes it one of the few family options that still works after dinner.
The space: A 500 m² interactive hall at Radnóti Miklós utca 18 in District XIII. Show the smartphone ticket at the entrance.

best_for.pick_html: for a rainy afternoon or a late evening because one €15.50 ticket lets you play up to 150 machines until midnight, with re-entry.
best_for.skip_html: if your kids are too young to play pinball or you want a quiet, calm visit: it is a flickering hall full of machines.

items.a: Entry ticket with re-entry bracelet for the night.
No minimum age or child price stated. Away from the main sights, in District XIII. Flickering arcade-style hall.
Machines are there to be played, not just looked at. Up to 150 playable machines on one ticket. Re-entry all night with a bracelet.

What to bring: The listing asks for comfortable shoes and warm clothing for the 1.5 km trail at Palatinus.
Paying on site: The venue is cashless, so bring a card for anything you buy on site. Tickets are delivered after booking and you present them at the venue.
Not suitable for: People with epilepsy. The trail is built around more than 200 light installations.

best_for.pick_html: for families who want a story-themed walk because the 1.5 km Alice in Wonderland trail packs more than 200 light installations into one €23 ticket.

title.text: Budapest Eye: skip-the-line ticket for the Ferris wheel

pills.pop_html: The ride: At least 3 full rotations in about 8 minutes, in an enclosed cabin, above the rooftops of the historic centre. Ride by day, at sunset or after dark.
Skip the line: The ticket gets you past the standard queue, and you can use it at any time during opening hours on your chosen day.
Families: A private cabin is only guaranteed if you buy 4 tickets, the cabin's maximum. For a family of four that is about €148. Children under 14 may only ride with a companion.
Opening hours: Monday to Thursday 11:00–23:00, Friday and Saturday 11:00–24:00, Sunday 11:00–23:00, every day of the year. Bring an ID card (a copy is accepted).

best_for.pick_html: for families of four who want the city from above in one short, central stop, because 4 tickets guarantee your own cabin and the wheel stays open until 23:00 or midnight.
best_for.skip_html: if you want a long activity for the money: it is about 8 minutes, so per minute it is the priciest thing on this page.

items.a: Priority access, a ride of about 8 minutes, panoramic views from an enclosed cabin, flexible access during opening hours.
About 8 minutes for €37 a person. Not suitable for people with vertigo. ID card needed.

pills.pop_html: What you get: Time to pet and interact with the museum's resident cats in a calm setting. Cats nap during the day, so nobody can promise when each will be in the mood to play.
Age rule: The minimum age is 8 for the comfort of the cats and guests. Strollers and baby carriages are not allowed, and the museum is not suitable for wheelchair users.
For kids: A corner with colouring equipment to draw cat art, Egyptian and Japanese photo walls, short films and a tablet quiz: score high enough and you pick a souvenir from the gift shop.
House rules: Remove your shoes (indoor slippers are provided) and disinfect your hands before petting. No dogs, no flash photography, no noise.

best_for.pick_html: for animal-loving kids aged 8 and up because €12.60 buys 1.5 hours with the resident cats plus a colouring corner and a quiz with a prize.
best_for.skip_html: if you have a child under 8 or a stroller with you: neither is allowed in.

items.a: Children under 8, wheelchair users; no strollers or baby carriages.

title.text: Budapest: Budapest Retro Interactive Museum Ticket

pills.pop_html: The highlight: A Soviet-made Lada police car turned into a simulator: you patrol a virtual Gazdagrét, a Budapest housing estate. There are also nine motorcycles and three vintage Soviet cars, including a black Volga.
Hands-on: Read real communist-era news broadcasts in a period studio with two working TV cameras, try on vintage outfits in an interactive mirror and walk through a typical 1970s–80s flat.
Size: Three floors of themed rooms with thousands of real objects, plus a room on Hungary's 1980 space mission with a spacesuit. Plan 1–2 hours.
After the visit: A retro bistro with a jukebox serving coffee, drinks and pastries, plus a souvenir shop. Food and drink are not part of the ticket.

best_for.pick_html: for families with teenagers because the Lada simulator, news studio and dress-up mirror make history something they do, not read, for about €16.
best_for.skip_html: if your kids are very young: the communist-era theme and newsreaders mean more to older children and adults.

items.a: Museum entry (faster entry when buying online).
Theme lands best with older kids. Price varies by day (weekday discounts for students). Bistro food and drinks cost extra.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

pills.pop_html: Star set: A 5 cubic metre pool of sugar pearls to jump into for photos, plus flamingo and unicorn sets.
Size: A 400 m², two-storey space with 11 rooms and more than 15 photo spots built so you can shoot from any angle.
Timing: The ticket is valid for 1 hour, so it fits between sights without eating your afternoon. Check starting times when you book.
Access: Not suitable for wheelchair users. Alcohol is not allowed inside.

best_for.pick_html: for tweens and teens who want photos to show friends, because 11 colourful rooms and a sugar-pearl pool fill an hour for €15.
best_for.skip_html: if your kids are not into posing for photos: there is little to do here beyond the sets.

items.q: How long is the ticket valid?

items.a: One-hour ticket. Fun depends on enjoying photos. Not suitable for wheelchair users.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

title.text: Budapest: Family Walking Tour with Mini Sculptures

pills.pop_html: What kids do: Hunt for Budapest's hidden mini-sculptures, including a lonely teddy bear and a little frog, and solve riddles on the way. You also get a checklist map to find more spots on your own afterwards.
Your guide: Led by a children's book author, with stories of the first Hungarian king, a princess in house slippers, Sultan Suleiman and Nikola Tesla.
Tech: An AR introduction and a final AR photo session using the tour book "The Princess, the Artist, and the Three Coins". Bring a fully charged smartphone.
Language: The tour is listed in Russian. The route is pushchair-friendly and accessible, and a seasonal treat (chocolate on cooler days) is included for each child.

best_for.pick_html: for Russian-speaking families with younger kids because the 2-hour route is pushchair-friendly and turns the old town into a riddle and sculpture hunt.
best_for.skip_html: if you need an English-language tour: this one is listed in Russian only.

items.a: 2-hour interactive tour by a children's book author, AR intro and photo session, games, quizzes and riddles, seasonal sweet treat for children, checklist map.
